statement: Cyclotomic centralizers of sections and germs over finitely generated characteristic-zero fields are trivial or unique cusp inertia; the same dichotomy holds for closed subgroups projecting openly to the cyclotomic kernel.
limitations: Fixed-point existence is not asserted.

statement: Every morphism to an elementary hyperbolic polycurve satisfies both geometric and arithmetic readings of F1(b).
limitations: Necessary direction only.

statement: F1 for a point is exactly F2 after removal of cusp packets; all cusp-factor maps fail b; units construct such maps; openness removes point and cusp sections alike.
limitations: An equivalence of surjectivity assertions, not a proof of their truth.

statement: Open arithmetic homomorphisms from normal varieties to a hyperbolic curve over a number field are exactly dominant morphisms, and satisfy b.
limitations: Target is a curve.

statement: An explicit smooth ample surface H in C^3 is nondominant but induces an arithmetic fundamental-group isomorphism.
limitations: Refutes open-image dominance in higher dimension; does not prove full F1.

statement: The unrestricted higher-dimensional sufficiency and full field reduction remain unproved. F.31 completes the requested infinite-index dichotomy using the supplied local theorem, and F.30 proves the universal curve-target reduction.
sources: Bresciani On the section conjecture over fields of finite type
limitations: The failed purely global elasticity approach is recorded as an attempted route, not the current status of F(b)(5).

statement: At most one fixed pro-point exists under the cyclotomic-kernel restriction, and its fixed set equals the full section's fixed set; the point/section dictionary identifies F2 with B.
limitations: Existence remains the section-conjecture assertion.

statement: The literally stated finite-group fixed-point assertion fails for G=1 and orientation-reversing reflection; nontrivial finite faithful orientation-preserving disk isometry groups have one fixed interior point.
limitations: An arbitrary outer action must first be realized; stated replacement retains nontriviality and orientation.

statement: Every functionwise continuous semilinear B-prime action preserves a finite hyperbolic quotient and is induced by a continuous section.
limitations: The abstract-action clause without continuity is unresolved.

statement: The cyclotomic absolute-Galois extension of every number field has no splitting over any open cyclotomic subgroup, even abstractly.
limitations: None.

statement: Invariant classes of sections over the cyclotomic kernel extend precisely when their normalizer quotient extension splits; cuspidal obstruction is the explicit transgression cocycle.
limitations: The general obstruction is a nonabelian extension-splitting class; the additive H2 formula is for a cusp.

statement: The tangential class of 1+i over Q(mu_infinity) is invariant but does not descend to Q; its computed transgression has exact order two.
limitations: Uses a fixed rational cusp and compatible tangent origin.

statement: In transcendence degree one, nonzero cyclotomic centralizer is equivalent to a rational-place decomposition section; scan127 formulas are false with L and true with U.
limitations: Does not prove every section has nonzero centralizer.

statement: Universal curve cuspidalization after all finitely generated base extensions is equivalent to geometric-or-cuspidal sections; the two cited Bresciani references are one paper.
limitations: The K(t) base change is essential to the cited implication.

statement: General birational lifting and arbitrary-rank compatible valuation reconstruction, and affine higher-dimensional devissage, remain unproved.
limitations: F.28 supplies the full proper-base induction, including an affine final fibre. Affine intermediate bases with cuspidal projected sections and compatible invariant valuations from all one-variable restrictions remain unresolved.

statement: For every splitting, a smooth realizing residue action is equivalent to potentially good marked reduction; stable bad reduction excludes realization after every finite residue extension.
limitations: Full profinite group and characteristic-zero residue field; separate push-prompt tasks are not silently included.

statement: The normal-line Chern class controls the injected cusp extension; geometric frames embed in all splittings, with explicit tangent/conormal sign comparison.
limitations: Smooth finite-type Q-base and injected normal inertia are retained.

statement: Cocycle twists act transitively on abstract local section classes; ambient cusp packet injection determines a completed coordinate after choosing its tangent origin.
limitations: A coordinate is not canonical without the origin.

statement: Everywhere locally geometric global Kummer classes are K* times completed global units; their quotient by K* is completed units modulo units; for Q the criterion is exact.
limitations: Local predicates mean actual local multiplicative classes at every finite place and local units almost everywhere.

statement: Powers of one infinite-order unit do not exhaust the nonglobal locally geometric classes; exact replacement is F.19 and associated idele classes with matching real signs lie in the identity component.
limitations: No canonical archimedean magnitudes are assigned.

statement: Completed rational ideles equal Qhat* times Zhat*; restricted local families have a unique decomposition using the real sign, and the unit coordinate is the exact fixed-cusp gluing obstruction.
sources: Direct idele factorization and Kummer restriction
limitations: Requires per-modulus finite support of valuations, every place including infinity, one rational cusp, and common tangent origin.

statement: Arbitrary compatible local families need not be completed ideles; b_p=p is a counterexample, and omitting the real place destroys factor uniqueness.
limitations: F.21 states and proves the corrected domain.

statement: In a smooth marked trait, uniformizer specialization of a point approaching a cusp gives the leading-coefficient tangent class; all geometric tangents occur, with exact uniformizer-change formula.
limitations: The smooth marked trait, chosen residue coefficient field, and uniformizer data are explicit.

statement: A formula using only the tripod automorphisms or the entries of a GT pair selecting all ordinary tangent parameters remains unresolved; F.45 supplies an intrinsic global criterion allowing two open Hom maps from an ambient open subgroup.
limitations: The automorphism-only GT formula is not inferred from the broader two-open-Hom criterion proved in F.45.

statement: Every-rank tame inertia character group, primewise ranks and noncanonical splitting; exact inertia normalizer is the decomposition group of the coarsening by the largest divisible convex subgroup.
sources: Kuhlmann Theorem 1.2, Corollary 2.9; Hensel chapter Theorem 9.44, Corollary 9.45
limitations: No existence of an invariant valuation for an arbitrary arithmetic section is inferred.

statement: An algebraic-residue valuation supplies a decomposition section over an open G_K subgroup exactly when its residue extension is finite; explicit DVR of Q(x,y) with infinite multiquadratic residue refutes the unqualified assertion; restriction to one-variable subfields is proved.
limitations: Scan 126 finite qualifier visually checked; scan 124 image unavailable in supplied selection, its insertion is reported by the transcription.

statement: For a one-variable function field, birational decomposition assertion a together with lifting b for every hyperbolic open over every finite extension is equivalent to F2 for all these opens; both lifting directions and inverse-limit compatibility are proved.
limitations: This is the requested exact equivalence of assertions, not a proof of their common universal truth.

statement: The universal curve-lifting assertion over all finitely generated characteristic-zero fields implies lifting for hyperbolic polycurves whose tower is proper except possibly at the final stage.
limitations: Affine intermediate bases with cuspidal projected sections are not covered; no change of domain from G_K to G_K(B) is assumed.

statement: A point-theoretic arithmetic map from any smooth geometrically connected variety over a number field or a finite p-adic extension to a hyperbolic curve is open or is a constant point-section map. For proper curve targets F1(b) is automatic, and all-source F1 is equivalent to point-section surjectivity over all finite extensions.
sources: Carlson–Stix Proposition C and Proposition 3.17 in its hyperbolic-target range
limitations: The map-level dichotomy retains the point-theoretic hypothesis. The broader nonhyperbolic wording of the cited body proposition is not used.

statement: Universal F2 over number fields is equivalent to F1 for hyperbolic curve targets and arbitrary smooth connected finite-type sources. The forward comparison forces every non-open map to have trivial geometric image or geometric image in one cusp inertia, using a high-genus target cover, fixed-source genus bounds, and exact cusp-fibre coset maps.
limitations: The common global surjectivity assertion remains unproved. F.31 separately supplies the open-or-trivial dichotomy from b using the stipulated local theorem.

statement: Using the stipulated local p-adic section theorem, every arithmetic homomorphism from a smooth geometrically connected variety to a hyperbolic curve over a finitely generated characteristic-zero field has geometric image open, trivial, or nontrivial in one cusp inertia. In the last case the entire arithmetic image is cuspidal, so F1(b) forces open or trivial geometric image.
sources: Supplied OpenAI p-adic section theorem, Theorem 1.1, and T1
Carlson–Stix Proposition 3.17 in the hyperbolic-target range
B.39: checked explicit countable finite-gerbe descent extends the trichotomy to every sub-p-adic field
limitations: The local section theorem is an explicitly stipulated unrefereed October 2026 input; this return does not claim its independent full verification. Global point-section surjectivity in the trivial-image branch is still F2.

statement: Exact higher-dimensional Hom and Isom ranges are derived from Hoshi, Schmidt–Stix, and the sharpened HSS relative theorem, retaining flatness, connected geometric generic fibre, and surjectivity of the smooth locus; all open maps satisfy b.
sources: HSS sharp final theorem and its proof
limitations: The relative homotopy datum and all source hypotheses are retained. HSS is an unrefereed supplied preprint.

statement: A smooth ample curve in a product of two hyperbolic curves gives the minimal-dimensional counterexample to open-image dominance; open homomorphisms to products reconstruct coordinatewise, and universal F1 for product targets is equivalent to curve F2.
limitations: The counterexample refutes dominance from openness; it does not refute geometric reconstruction. The displayed curve has non-finitely-generated kernel.

statement: Reconstruction for the remaining non-product surface targets with infinitely generated kernel and no applicable relative flat presentation remains unresolved.
limitations: Base-curve reconstruction and the relative fibre-product map are constructed. Openness on the geometric generic fibre and extension at missing smooth fibres are the exact unresolved steps.

statement: The corrected 1981 boundary category, dominant curve F1, admissible sections, F2, the letter and postscript, fixed subgroups, and axioms 1–6 on geometric objects are related by explicit functors, restrictions, and packet complements.
limitations: Intrinsic realization and axioms 5–6 for arbitrary abstract actions retain the unresolved status recorded in Part B.

statement: The exact Bresciani number-field-to-finitely-generated ranges are proved via the cited reductions; a generic proper-family section yields a non-open group map satisfying b whose geometric reconstruction is precisely the missing general field-reduction step.
sources: Bresciani Theorem B, Corollaries A–C and Corollary 3.4
limitations: General F2 reduction without a cover mapping to a constant abelian variety remains open; no Bombieri–Lang or Tate–Shafarevich conjecture is assumed proved.

statement: Number-field F2 implies the one-variable birational section assertion over every finitely generated characteristic-zero field; every section already admitting a birational lift is consequently point or cusp under that exact implication of assertions.
limitations: This is an implication between requested assertions. The quotient from the absolute Galois group does not construct a lift of an arbitrary section.

statement: Carlson–Corwin inductive cuspidality is tower-independent exactly with the universal curve section assertion; the checked comparison from boundary-local cuspidality to the closure of the inductive set is one-way.
sources: Carlson–Corwin Proposition B and prop:fibinclusion, with proofs
limitations: The reverse inclusion and birational lifting of an arbitrary section with cuspidal base projection are unproved; the supplied preprint is unrefereed.

statement: A specified four-puncture diagram transports the parameter-1 cusp section to any rational parameter t, and the exact change of normalized GT conjugator is f_sigma^c=f_sigma*x^(-c(sigma)).
limitations: The diagram retains the cross-ratio t; the coordinate test retains its Kummer cocycle. Pure intrinsic recognition in one tripod remains open.

statement: Two distinct valuations of Q(z,x,y), each with residue Q and value group Z lex Q, have identical nonzero inertia, normalized by one section that does not preserve one of the valuations.
sources: FLAGGED_149 F149-ZD5 and its full construction F149-D3
limitations: Refutes uniqueness defined through inertia normalization and the inference from normalization to actual valuation preservation; it does not assert two distinct actually invariant valuations.

statement: A discontinuous quadratic twist of the rational 1/2 point action on the universal tripod covering admits no continuously descended finite étale quotient on any open arithmetic subgroup, while retaining a unique cyclotomic fixed pro-point.
sources: Explicit dense-kernel linear functional on a multiquadratic Galois quotient
limitations: Refutes the finite-form reduction without continuity; it does not refute fixed-point existence for arbitrary abstract actions.

statement: For a hyperbolic surface fibration with good marked reduction at a selected base cusp, the pullback extension is the fibre product of the special-fibre extension and the base cusp extension; every point-or-cusp residue section has an explicit rank-two birational lift. Universal curve lifting therefore extends to this affine-base range.
sources: Smooth marked specialization and the hyperbolic fibre sequence
limitations: Bad marked reduction at the selected base cusp is not covered. The universal implication is between the assertions expressly requested, not an assumption of global section surjectivity.

statement: Exact comparison of normal tubes, Chern transgression, finite-root inertia kernels, covering sub-germs, stable-tower full inertia, and FLAGGED C1–C6/C8/C9 through their actual Kummer and normal-specialization maps.
sources: LM5 F.21–F.23, F.35, F.39, F.48 (proofs read)
Carchedi–Scherotzke–Sibilla–Talpo Theorem A and Corollary5.5 (primary opened)
limitations: The stable/toroidal compatibility and geometric-section premises are retained; arbitrary compactifications can have nonzero full local inertia kernel.

statement: A point or cusp section on the τ-twisted residue curve at a potentially good base cusp lifts through a rank-two decomposition group and hence birationally; universal curve lifting therefore implies surface lifting in this potentially-good-boundary range.
sources: F.16 stable-model descent and full finite-cover comparison
limitations: The implication between universal lifting assertions is proved; universal curve lifting and the genuinely bad marked-reduction case are not asserted.

statement: Over every number field, the geometric tangential cusp sections of the arithmetic tripod are exactly those satisfying a uniform two-open-Hom relation from one ambient open subgroup, with inertia degrees one and two and equal section images. Each specified t is uniquely selected by a concrete such relation; satisfaction after finite extension descends.
sources: Mochizuki relative open Hom theorem, as checked in F.4 and A:relative-hom
Scherr–Zieve, Separated Belyi maps, Theorem 1.1 (primary proof opened)
Part B cusp packet injectivity and local root-cover formula
limitations: The relation quantifies over two open homomorphisms from an ambient open subgroup. A formula using only the original tripod automorphisms or a GT pair is not asserted; no section-surjectivity or stipulated local theorem is used.

statement: The injective-open-Hom (equivalently finite-etale) restriction of F.45 selects exactly the rational tangent parameters 16 and -16. The same conclusion holds for the union of all tests with unequal positive local degrees; over a number field all common section images are ordinary tangents in 16 times its roots of unity. Thus the concrete replacement by finite-cover commensurations fails at t=2.
sources: Calegari–Dimitrov–Tang, JAMS38 (2025), equation(1.0.2), p628 (primary author offprint opened)
Elementary commensurator proof via parabolic fixed points and commensurable lattices
Explicit elimination for arbitrary unequal local degrees and the torsion computation in the power completion of K*

statement: On the universal covering of the same tripod over Q(i), an explicit abstract semilinear action remains discontinuous on every open subgroup of the cyclotomic kernel. It admits no continuously descended finite-type quotient that is a connected pro-etale covering, even after such a restriction, and nevertheless has exactly one cyclotomic-kernel fixed pro-point.
sources: Independent Gaussian-prime Kummer proof in F.47
limitations: This strengthens the explicit failure of continuous finite-form descent to the actual cyclotomic-kernel domain of B-prime. Universal fixed-point existence for arbitrary abstract actions remains unresolved.
